messages:
ria: Quick bakeoff update — ran short GPTQ sweep across three families (Llama2-70b, Mistral-8x, Qwen-7B) to compare GPTQ vs AWQ vs INT8 profiles on our standard instr-follow + long-context evals. TL;DR: tradeoffs vary by family, no one-size-fits-all.

sam: Nice, can you drop configs and top-line numbers? :eyes:

ria: Sure. Configs we used:
- GPTQ: 4-bit per-tensor, fused quant, KV-caching intact
- AWQ: 8-bit asymmetric per-channel recommended flags
- INT8: naive activation/int8 work with calibration set (1000 samples)
- FP8 baseline for perf/quality anchor

Top-line deltas vs FP8 baseline (instr-follow accuracy / long-context QA EM):
- Llama2-70b GPTQ4: -1.8% / -2.2% ; throughput +2.5x
- Llama2-70b AWQ8: -0.7% / -1.1% ; throughput +1.6x
- Mistral-8x GPTQ4: -4.5% / -6.0% (noticeable hallucination on long prompts) ; throughput +3.1x
- Mistral-8x AWQ8: -2.0% / -2.8% ; throughput +1.9x
- Qwen-7B GPTQ4: -0.9% / -1.4% ; throughput +2.2x
- Qwen-7B AWQ8: -0.3% / -0.5% ; throughput +1.4x
- INT8 across families: mixed; generally better than GPTQ on Mistral long-context but worse than AWQ on Qwen instr-follow

jules: Whoa Mistral GPTQ4 lost 6% on long-context EM — any hypothesis?

ria: Two likely causes: 1) KV-cache layout differences in Mistral variants interact poorly with our GPTQ packing (we see more small-token drift), 2) calibration samples underrepresented longer sequences so attention scaling drifts.

ankur: Did you try longer calibration or per-head calibration hack we prototyped?

ria: Quick test: per-head calibration on Mistral reduced long-context EM drop from -6.0% to -3.1% but increased quantization noise on shorter instruction tasks (instr-follow recovered to -2.6%). So better but not perfect.

ci-bot: build 2026-03-01T10:12Z: eval suite run finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/gptq-bakeoff/1967890123/* (profiles, diffs, token-level traces).

sam: Any callouts on latency/99p? We care about tail for product.

ria: 99p token latency (on our dedicated 8xA100 profile):
- Llama2-70b GPTQ4: 1.2s/token 99p (was 0.9s FP8) — spikes due to cache rehydration on some prompts
- Mistral-8x GPTQ4: 0.9s/token 99p (FP8 was 0.6s)
- Qwen-7B GPTQ4: 0.45s/token 99p (FP8 0.38s)
AWQ8 tends to have lower variance than GPTQ4 at similar mean throughput.

jules: Sounds like AWQ is safer as a deployable default for now, GPTQ needs more family-specific tuning. Agree?

ria: Yeah. Recommendation for rollout profiles:
- Qwen-7B: AWQ8 default; GPTQ4 as an opt-in experimental profile for cheap inference with canary tests
- Llama2-70b: AWQ8 default; GPTQ only if we can apply per-head calibration and accept small instr-follow regressions
- Mistral-8x: Do NOT default to GPTQ4 until we solve KV/cache packing + calibration; AWQ8 or INT8 with heavy calibration are safer

ankur: For Dedicated customers that want cheapest unit cost, we should publish a guidance doc with exact calibration recipe and a small prompt-set eval. Can you stub that?

ria: Will do. Plan: put a short canonical calibration script + 500-sequence calibration bundle and a 200-prompt long-context smoke test in the repo. Also include token-level diff traces for the Mistral failure modes.

sam: Can you paste the calibration command you'll use? makes it easy for infra to wire up CI.

ria: calibration run example:
```bash
python quant/calibrate.py --model mistral-8x --method per-head --dataset s3://redwood-calib/mistral/500-seqs.jsonl 
--out artifacts/mistral-perhead-calib.pkl
```

ci-bot: note: added job gptq-bakeoff-calib-196789 to Jenkins queue.

jules: One more ask — include a tiny eval that measures instruction hallucination (we saw a spike) so product can decide fallback thresholds.

ria: Good call. Adding an "instr-hallucination" suite (50 hard prompts) to the rollouts checklist. I'll link artifacts when uploaded.

sam: Thanks — please put the per-family recommended config + brief pros/cons in the PR so solutions eng can use it for customer consultations. :+1:
